/**
 * EQC-1 (issue #1152, epic #1038) — equipment_catalogue bucket re-partition.
 *
 * Maps every live `equipment_catalogue` document from the OLD four-bucket
 * taxonomy to the NEW five-value one:
 *
 *   weapon    → combat_gear   (weapon-shaped: damage_mod/damage_type/weapon_type)
 *   armour    → combat_gear   (armour-shaped: armour_value/defence_penalty)
 *   equipment → skill_gear    (unchanged meaning — skill_domain + bonus_dice)
 *   asset     → container     ("assets are containers... no stat-stacking
 *                              on the asset itself" — epic #1038)
 *
 * `combat_gear` absorbs both old weapon and armour buckets, distinguished at
 * read time by WHICH stat fields are populated on the item — not by a new
 * subtype field. This mirrors the epic's own wording ("combat gear
 * (weapons/armour, distinct stat fields)") and needs no new schema field.
 *
 * WHY THIS CANNOT SHIP INDEPENDENTLY OF THE SCHEMA CHANGE. Unlike
 * backfill-free-grants.js's union-sum runtime guard, nothing in this codebase
 * reads BOTH the old and new bucket vocabulary simultaneously (a deliberate
 * choice — see the EQC-1 story's "Migration shape" decision, atomic not
 * dual-support). So an un-migrated document is invisible to every consumer
 * (armourDefencePenalty, roll calculator weapon/skill chips, sheet renderer,
 * DT form dropdown) the moment the new-taxonomy-aware code lands. This script
 * and the schema/consumer changes in the same story MUST land together on
 * this branch before merge — there is no safe "schema first, migrate later"
 * window here, unlike the free-grants case.
 *
 * Idempotent: re-running matches zero docs the second time (every document's
 * `bucket` is already one of the new five values after the first apply).
 * Dry-run default, mirrors backfill-free-grants.js's own CLI shape.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   # preview (default — no writes):
 *   node server/scripts/migrate-eqc1-bucket-taxonomy.mjs
 *
 *   # apply:
 *   node server/scripts/migrate-eqc1-bucket-taxonomy.mjs --apply
 *
 *   # target the test DB:
 *   MONGODB_DB=tm_suite_test node server/scripts/migrate-eqc1-bucket-taxonomy.mjs --apply
 *
 * Locally, run from `server/` so cwd-relative `dotenv/config` picks up
 * `server/.env`. On Render env vars are pre-set (no-op).
 */

import 'dotenv/config';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'url';
import { connectDb, getCollection, closeDb } from '../db.js';

/** Old bucket → new bucket. The one-to-one mapping this whole script exists to apply. */
export const BUCKET_MAP = Object.freeze({
  weapon: 'combat_gear',
  armour: 'combat_gear',
  equipment: 'skill_gear',
  asset: 'container',
});

const NEW_BUCKETS = new Set(['combat_gear', 'skill_gear', 'tool_utility', 'narrative', 'container']);

/**
 * Compute the migration plan for a single catalogue document. Pure — no DB
 * access, no module-level state.
 *
 * @param {object} doc - an equipment_catalogue document
 * @returns {{ touched: boolean, fromBucket: string|undefined, toBucket: string|undefined, reason: string|null }}
 */
export function planBucketMigration(doc) {
  if (!doc || typeof doc !== 'object') {
    return { touched: false, fromBucket: undefined, toBucket: undefined, reason: 'malformed document' };
  }
  const from = doc.bucket;
  // EQC-1 review patch (#1152, Codex external review Low finding): a
  // non-string `bucket` (e.g. `['weapon']`) would otherwise reach
  // `BUCKET_MAP[from]` and JS's implicit property-key coercion would stringify
  // it to `'weapon'`, silently normalising a malformed document instead of
  // flagging it for human review per this function's own "flag rather than
  // guess" policy. Reject any non-string bucket explicitly, before either
  // lookup.
  if (typeof from !== 'string') {
    return { touched: false, fromBucket: from, toBucket: undefined, reason: `bucket is not a string (got ${Array.isArray(from) ? 'array' : typeof from})` };
  }
  if (NEW_BUCKETS.has(from)) {
    return { touched: false, fromBucket: from, toBucket: from, reason: null };
  }
  const to = BUCKET_MAP[from];
  if (!to) {
    // Neither a known old value nor a known new one — flag rather than guess.
    return { touched: false, fromBucket: from, toBucket: undefined, reason: `unrecognised bucket value "${from}"` };
  }
  return { touched: true, fromBucket: from, toBucket: to, reason: null };
}

/**
 * Drive the migration against MongoDB. Returns the aggregate summary.
 *
 * @param {object} [opts]
 * @param {boolean} [opts.dryRun]
 * @param {boolean} [opts.log]
 */
export async function migrate(opts = {}) {
  const { dryRun = true, log = true } = opts;
  const col = getCollection('equipment_catalogue');
  const docs = await col.find({}).toArray();

  const totals = {
    scanned: docs.length,
    touched: 0,
    written: 0,
    perMapping: Object.create(null),
    unrecognised: [],
    failedAt: null,
  };

  // EQC-1 review patch (#1152, Codex external review Medium finding): the
  // original version incremented `totals.touched` and logged the summary
  // ONLY after the full loop completed, so a mid-loop `updateOne` failure
  // (e.g. a transient Mongo disconnect) threw before an operator saw ANY
  // record of what had already been written. `written` now tracks
  // confirmed-successful writes separately from `touched` (planned writes),
  // and the summary logs from inside a catch block too, so a partial-apply
  // state is always visible even on failure.
  try {
    for (const doc of docs) {
      const plan = planBucketMigration(doc);
      if (plan.reason && !plan.touched) {
        totals.unrecognised.push({ id: String(doc._id), name: doc.name || '(unnamed)', bucket: plan.fromBucket });
        continue;
      }
      if (!plan.touched) continue;

      const key = `${plan.fromBucket} → ${plan.toBucket}`;
      totals.perMapping[key] = (totals.perMapping[key] || 0) + 1;
      totals.touched += 1;

      if (!dryRun) {
        await col.updateOne({ _id: doc._id }, { $set: { bucket: plan.toBucket, updated_at: new Date().toISOString() } });
        totals.written += 1;
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    totals.failedAt = { scannedSoFar: totals.touched, writtenSoFar: totals.written, error: String(err && err.message || err) };
    if (log) logSummary(totals, dryRun);
    throw err;
  }

  if (log) logSummary(totals, dryRun);
  return totals;
}

export function logSummary(totals, dryRun) {
  const verb = dryRun ? '[DRY RUN] would touch' : 'touched';
  console.log(`Scanned ${totals.scanned} catalogue item(s); ${verb} ${totals.touched}.`);
  if (totals.failedAt) {
    console.log(`\nFAILED mid-run: ${totals.failedAt.writtenSoFar} write(s) confirmed committed before the error; ` +
      `${totals.failedAt.scannedSoFar - totals.failedAt.writtenSoFar} more were planned but not yet attempted or did not complete. ` +
      `This script is idempotent — re-run it (dry-run first) to pick up where it left off, rather than assuming a full re-apply is needed.`);
    console.log(`Error: ${totals.failedAt.error}`);
  }
  if (Object.keys(totals.perMapping).length) {
    console.log('Per-mapping:');
    for (const [k, n] of Object.entries(totals.perMapping)) console.log(`  ${k.padEnd(24)} ${n}`);
  }
  if (totals.unrecognised.length) {
    console.log(`\nUNRECOGNISED bucket values (${totals.unrecognised.length}) — SKIPPED, need human review:`);
    for (const u of totals.unrecognised) console.log(`  ${u.name} (${u.id}): bucket="${u.bucket}"`);
  }
}

export async function main(argv = process.argv) {
  const dryRun = !argv.includes('--apply');
  console.log(`Mode: ${dryRun ? 'DRY RUN (read only; pass --apply to write)' : 'APPLY (will write)'}`);
  console.log(`Target DB: ${process.env.MONGODB_DB || 'tm_suite'}`);
  console.log('');

  await connectDb();
  try {
    await migrate({ dryRun });
  } finally {
    await closeDb();
  }

  console.log('\nIdempotency check (after --apply): re-run with no flag and confirm "touched 0".');
}

// Auto-run only when invoked directly (not when imported by a test).
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) {
  main().catch(err => { console.error(err); process.exit(1); });
}

-### [Pass 1] Ambiguous combat-gear rows are silently treated as weapons
+### Pass 1
+
+#### [Pass 1] A checked tweak request follows the row, not the selected catalogue item
+
+- **Severity**: Medium
+- **File:line**: `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2781`, `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:5609`
+- **Triggering input or sequence**: In one equipment row, select tweakable item A, check `equipment_${n}_tweak`, then change the same row's catalogue dropdown to a different tweakable item B. The delegated change handler calls `collectResponses()` before rerendering, so it saves `'true'`; `renderEquipmentRow` then restores that value solely from the row-number key.
+- **Observable consequence**: Item B is immediately rendered with a checked tweak request even though the player only checked the control while item A was selected. The submitted request can therefore ask the ST to tweak a different item without a fresh affirmative action by the player.
+- **Confidence**: High from the control flow visible in the diff; whether product scope considers row-level carryover acceptable cannot be determined without the story.
+
+#### [Pass 1] Dual-shaped combat gear is silently and irreversibly treated as a weapon
+
+- **Severity**: Medium
+- **File:line**: `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:384`
+- **Triggering input or sequence**: Pass a `combat_gear` entry with any populated weapon discriminator (`weapon_type`, `damage_mod`, or `damage_type`) and any populated armour discriminator (`armour_value` or `defence_penalty`).
+- **Observable consequence**: `equipmentTweakableField` returns `damage_mod`; there is no route to request an `armour_value` tweak for the same entry. If the catalogue/admin layer permits hybrid or legacy rows, this is a silent loss of one plausible interpretation.
+- **Confidence**: Medium. The precedence is certain from the diff; whether mutual exclusivity is guaranteed elsewhere must be checked in Pass 2.
+

/**
 * DT submission MINIMAL-completeness check (ADR-003 §Q3, §Q8).
 *
 * Single source of truth for "is this player above the minimum-complete bar
 * this cycle?". Lives in its own module so it can be imported client-side
 * (downtime-form lifecycle) and, in a future Q7 server-side validation pass,
 * by the API without dragging form code along.
 *
 * Pure ESM. No DOM. No `document` / `window` / `localStorage` / `fetch`.
 *
 * MINIMAL set per ADR §Q2:
 *   court + personal_story (reduced) + feeding (simplified)
 *   + 1 project + regency-if-regent
 *
 * Each rule below mirrors the §Q8 spec and is inverted to drive the
 * banner's missing-pieces list (story #17 UI affordance #1).
 */

// dt-form.20 fix-up (Ma'at PR #98 review, bug 1): MINIMAL has no pool builder,
// so `_feed_disc` / `_feed_custom_*` stay empty when a player only fills the
// 5-field simplified form. The method-card pick still persists `_feed_method`,
// so include it as a method-set signal. Without this, hard-mirror per #17
// never unlocks for MINIMAL users — banner sticks even with all 5 fields set.
const FEEDING_POOL_KEYS = ['_feed_method', '_feed_disc', '_feed_custom_attr', '_feed_custom_skill', '_feed_custom_disc'];

function isNonEmptyString(v) {
  return typeof v === 'string' && v.trim().length > 0;
}

function _hasAnyGameRecount(responses) {
  // Any of game_recount_1..5 non-empty, or the legacy joined `game_recount`.
  for (let n = 1; n <= 5; n++) {
    if (isNonEmptyString(responses[`game_recount_${n}`])) return true;
  }
  return isNonEmptyString(responses.game_recount);
}

// Issue #939: Personal Story (Off-Screen Life) is now OPTIONAL. It was
// previously gated by a _hasPersonalStory() check here; that helper and its
// callers (isMinimalComplete + missingMinimumPieces) were removed so a blank
// Personal Story no longer holds a player's downtime XP credit.

function _hasFeedingTerritory(responses) {
  // feeding_territories is a JSON-stringified map of slug → state. Any slug
  // not 'none' counts as a chosen feeding territory.
  let grid;
  try { grid = JSON.parse(responses.feeding_territories || '{}'); } catch { return false; }
  if (!grid || typeof grid !== 'object') return false;
  return Object.values(grid).some(state => isNonEmptyString(state) && state !== 'none');
}

function _hasFeedingMethod(responses) {
  return FEEDING_POOL_KEYS.some(k => isNonEmptyString(responses[k]));
}

function _hasFeedingBloodType(responses) {
  let arr;
  try { arr = JSON.parse(responses._feed_blood_types || '[]'); } catch { return false; }
  return Array.isArray(arr) && arr.length > 0;
}

function _hasFeedingViolence(responses) {
  return isNonEmptyString(responses.feed_violence);
}

function _hasFeedingComplete(responses) {
  // dt-form.22: ROTE in a project slot does NOT satisfy the feeding rule.
  // Primary feeding (territory + method + blood type + violence) must be
  // filled independently. ROTE is captured under the `1 project slot`
  // MINIMAL rule (any non-empty `project_1_action`, including 'rote').
  return _hasFeedingTerritory(responses)
      && _hasFeedingMethod(responses)
      && _hasFeedingBloodType(responses)
      && _hasFeedingViolence(responses);
}

function _hasFirstProject(responses) {
  return isNonEmptyString(responses.project_1_action);
}

/**
 * @param {object} responses           — submission.responses bag
 * @param {object} [ctx]               — optional caller-side context
 * @param {boolean} [ctx.isRegent]      — true if the character owns a regent territory
 * @param {boolean} [ctx.regencyConfirmed] — true if the regent has confirmed feeding rights this cycle
 * @param {boolean} [ctx.attended]      — true if the character attended last game; defaults true so callers without attendance context are unaffected
 * @returns {boolean}
 */
export function isMinimalComplete(responses, ctx = {}) {
  if (!responses || typeof responses !== 'object') return false;
  const { isRegent = false, regencyConfirmed = false, attended = true } = ctx;

  if (attended && !_hasAnyGameRecount(responses)) return false;
  // Issue #939: Personal Story no longer gates minimum-complete (optional).
  if (!_hasFeedingComplete(responses)) return false;
  if (!_hasFirstProject(responses)) return false;
  if (isRegent && !regencyConfirmed) return false;
  return true;
}

/**
 * Inverts isMinimalComplete to drive the banner's missing-pieces list.
 *
 * @param {object} responses
 * @param {object} [ctx]
 * @returns {{section: string, label: string}[]}
 */
export function missingMinimumPieces(responses, ctx = {}) {
  const out = [];
  if (!responses || typeof responses !== 'object') {
    out.push({ section: 'court', label: 'Fill in your game recount' });
    out.push({ section: 'feeding', label: 'Pick a feeding territory, method, blood type, and Kiss/Violent toggle' });
    out.push({ section: 'projects', label: 'Pick an action for Project 1' });
    return out;
  }
  const { isRegent = false, regencyConfirmed = false, attended = true } = ctx;

  if (attended && !_hasAnyGameRecount(responses)) {
    out.push({ section: 'court', label: 'Game Recount: add at least one highlight from last session' });
  }

+# Adversarial review findings — EQC-4 (#1155)
+
+## High
+
+- None found.

+## Medium
+
+### [Pass 1] Ambiguous combat-gear rows are silently treated as weapons
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:390`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Pass an entry with `bucket: 'combat_gear'` and at least one populated weapon-shape field as well as at least one populated armour-shape field—for example, `{ bucket: 'combat_gear', damage_mod: 1, armour_value: 2 }`.
+- **Observable consequence:** `equipmentTweakableField` returns `damage_mod` immediately and provides no way to request the armour tweak. From the diff alone, mutual exclusivity is not established, so this is worth checking against the schema and catalogue-admin validation in Pass 2.
+- **Confidence:** Medium. The precedence is certain; whether a dual-shaped catalogue entry is possible is not knowable from the permitted Pass 1 material.
+
+### [Pass 1] A checked tweak request migrates to a different tweakable item in the same slot
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2781`, `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:5615`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Select tweakable item A in an equipment row, check its tweak checkbox, then change that row's catalogue dropdown directly to different tweakable item B.
+- **Observable consequence:** The delegated change handler first collects the row after the select has changed but while A's checked checkbox is still in the DOM. It therefore saves B's catalogue id together with `'true'`, then re-renders B with its checkbox checked. A request explicitly made for A silently becomes a request for B.
+- **Confidence:** High. The collect-before-render sequence and slot-only saved key are both explicit in the diff.
+
+### [Pass 1] `skill_gear` is declared tweakable even when its numeric stat is absent
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:394`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Call `equipmentTweakableField({ bucket: 'skill_gear' })`, or render a malformed/legacy skill-gear catalogue row without `bonus_dice`.
+- **Observable consequence:** The helper returns `'bonus_dice'` and the form offers a `+1 bonus_dice` request even though the function's contract and adjacent comment say tweakability requires a primary numeric bonus field. The combat branch validates shape, but the skill branch validates only the bucket.
+- **Confidence:** High that the function behaves this way; Medium that such malformed/legacy rows can reach the consumer, pending repository inspection.
+
+## Low
+
+### [Pass 1] The “only when tweakable” test does not prove conditional rendering
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `server/tests/issue-871-876-ecm-4-9-bundle.test.js:166`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Move the checkbox markup outside the `if (tweakField)` block while leaving it textually after `equipmentTweakableField(selectedEntry)` in the file.
+- **Observable consequence:** The test still passes even though every row would render the checkbox. It checks only that the gating call exists before the checkbox substring, so its title materially overstates the regression protection.
+- **Confidence:** High.
+
+### [Pass 1] The persistence test does not verify checkbox state is read
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `server/tests/issue-871-876-ecm-4-9-bundle.test.js:184`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Replace the implementation with any assignment to `responses[\`equipment_${n}_tweak\`]`, including a constant such as `''` or `'false'`.
+- **Observable consequence:** The test still passes although checked state is no longer persisted. Its title says it verifies persistence “from the checkbox DOM state,” but its sole regex asserts only that an assignment exists.
+- **Confidence:** High.

codex
Pass 2 is ready to freeze. The removal shift is correctly aligned, missing/deleted catalogue entries degrade cleanly, `dt-equip-cat` is unique and does not overlap later delegated routes, `equipmentSlots` counts only catalogue/name keys, and the raw tweak cost and `rawMax = cap + fixer` are algebraically comparable. The remaining findings are the hidden ST request, reachable malformed-shape behavior, the availability-6 boundary, and missing regression coverage for those cases.

# EQC-4 adversarial review findings

## High

### Pass 1

- None found.

## Medium

### Pass 1

#### [Pass 1] A checked tweak request follows the row, not the selected catalogue item

- **Severity**: Medium
- **File:line**: `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2781`, `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:5609`
- **Triggering input or sequence**: In one equipment row, select tweakable item A, check `equipment_${n}_tweak`, then change the same row's catalogue dropdown to a different tweakable item B. The delegated change handler calls `collectResponses()` before rerendering, so it saves `'true'`; `renderEquipmentRow` then restores that value solely from the row-number key.
- **Observable consequence**: Item B is immediately rendered with a checked tweak request even though the player only checked the control while item A was selected. The submitted request can therefore ask the ST to tweak a different item without a fresh affirmative action by the player.
- **Confidence**: High from the control flow visible in the diff; whether product scope considers row-level carryover acceptable cannot be determined without the story.

#### [Pass 1] Dual-shaped combat gear is silently and irreversibly treated as a weapon

- **Severity**: Medium
- **File:line**: `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:384`
- **Triggering input or sequence**: Pass a `combat_gear` entry with any populated weapon discriminator (`weapon_type`, `damage_mod`, or `damage_type`) and any populated armour discriminator (`armour_value` or `defence_penalty`).
- **Observable consequence**: `equipmentTweakableField` returns `damage_mod`; there is no route to request an `armour_value` tweak for the same entry. If the catalogue/admin layer permits hybrid or legacy rows, this is a silent loss of one plausible interpretation.
- **Confidence**: Medium. The precedence is certain from the diff; whether mutual exclusivity is guaranteed elsewhere must be checked in Pass 2.

## Low

### Pass 1

#### [Pass 1] Skill gear is declared tweakable even when it has no numeric bonus field

- **Severity**: Low
- **File:line**: `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:388`
- **Triggering input or sequence**: Call `equipmentTweakableField({ bucket: 'skill_gear' })`, or use a malformed/legacy skill-gear catalogue row with no `bonus_dice` value.
- **Observable consequence**: The function returns `bonus_dice` and the form offers a `+1 bonus_dice` request despite the function documentation saying it returns `null` when there is no tweakable numeric bonus. The new unit test only covers a skill-gear fixture where `bonus_dice` is present.
- **Confidence**: Medium pending the repository's schema/admin guarantees.

#### [Pass 1] Numeric-string availability is silently treated as zero

- **Severity**: Low
- **File:line**: `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:404`
- **Triggering input or sequence**: Call `tweakedAvailability` with a tweakable entry whose availability is a numeric string, for example `{ bucket: 'skill_gear', bonus_dice: 1, availability: '3' }`.
- **Observable consequence**: `Number.isInteger('3')` is false, so the reported tweak cost is `1` rather than `4`; the over-cap warning can consequently be suppressed. The tests cover a number and a missing value, but not the numeric-string boundary.
- **Confidence**: Medium pending confirmation of real catalogue-document types in Pass 2.

#### [Pass 1] The “ONLY when tweakable” render test does not prove conditional gating

- **Severity**: Low
- **File:line**: `server/tests/issue-871-876-ecm-4-9-bundle.test.js:164`
- **Triggering input or sequence**: Move or duplicate the checkbox markup into unconditional render code anywhere after the first textual occurrence of `equipmentTweakableField(selectedEntry)`, while leaving that function call present.
- **Observable consequence**: The test still passes because it checks only that the function-call text exists and that checkbox text occurs later in the file. A regression that shows the checkbox for non-tweakable items would not be caught despite the test title's “ONLY” claim.
- **Confidence**: High.

#### [Pass 1] The persistence test proves only that some assignment exists

- **Severity**: Low
- **File:line**: `server/tests/issue-871-876-ecm-4-9-bundle.test.js:180`
- **Triggering input or sequence**: Replace the right-hand side of the tweak response assignment with a constant or invert the checkbox state while retaining `responses[`equipment_${n}_tweak`] =`.
- **Observable consequence**: The test remains green even though checked/unchecked DOM state is no longer persisted correctly.
- **Confidence**: High.

#### [Pass 1] The availability-warning comparison cannot be unit-validated from the scoped diff

- **Severity**: Low
- **File:line**: `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:5610`
- **Triggering input or sequence**: Render any tweakable item near the character cap; the new code compares raw `entry.availability + 1` with the pre-existing `rawMax`, whose definition is outside the diff.
- **Observable consequence**: If `rawMax` is in effective/post-Fixer units rather than raw catalogue units, the warning threshold will be off by the Fixer adjustment. The diff alone is insufficient to decide whether this occurs.
- **Confidence**: Low until Pass 2 traces `rawMax`, `availabilityCap`, and `fixerReduction`.

#### [Pass 1] The delegated class trigger's exclusivity cannot be established from the diff

- **Severity**: Low
- **File:line**: `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2781`
- **Triggering input or sequence**: Change any element carrying `dt-equip-cat`; the new branch collects responses and rerenders the whole form, then returns.
- **Observable consequence**: If the class is reused, an unrelated change would spuriously rerender and the early return could suppress a later matching branch. The unchanged select markup and the rest of the large delegate are not in the diff, so exclusivity is not yet verifiable.
- **Confidence**: Low until Pass 2 searches the real file.

# Pass 2 — Edge Case Hunter (frozen before reading the story)

## High

### [Pass 2] The captured tweak request is invisible in the ST processing UI

- **Severity:** High
- **File:line:** `public/js/admin/downtime-views.js:1647`
- **Triggering input or sequence:** A player selects a tweakable catalogue item, checks `equipment_1_tweak`, and lets the form auto-save or submits it; an ST then opens that submission in the normal downtime processing UI.
- **Observable consequence:** The response bag retains `equipment_1_tweak: 'true'`, but `renderPlayerResponses` builds each equipment row from only catalogue id/name, quantity, and notes. The only repository references to the new response key are the player-form write/render/slot-shift sites, so the ST sees an ordinary equipment request and has no indication that the player requested a +1 stat tweak. The feature's own player copy says the ST will adjudicate it, but the ST-facing surface drops the signal.
- **Confidence:** High. The complete equipment renderer was inspected and a repository-wide source search found no downstream reader of `equipment_${n}_tweak`.

## Medium

### [Pass 2] Dual-shaped combat gear is supported by the catalogue editor but has only a weapon tweak path

- **Severity:** Medium
- **File:line:** `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:390`; `public/js/admin/equipment-catalogue-admin.js:32`
- **Triggering input or sequence:** An ST creates or edits `combat_gear` with both a weapon field and an armour field populated—for example, `damage_mod: 1` and `armour_value: 2`—then a player selects it in an equipment-acquisition row.
- **Observable consequence:** The admin module explicitly says both subsets may be populated “in principle,” renders all five weapon/armour inputs together, and performs no mutual-exclusivity validation. Nevertheless, `equipmentTweakableField` returns `damage_mod` at the first predicate and never offers an armour-value tweak. A supported catalogue row therefore loses one of its two plausible tweak choices by branch order alone.
- **Confidence:** High. Direct execution returned `damage_mod` for the dual-shaped fixture, and both the schema and admin form permit that fixture.

### [Pass 2] A checked request still migrates when the catalogue selection changes

- **Severity:** Medium
- **File:line:** `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2785`; `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:5613`
- **Triggering input or sequence:** In one row, select tweakable item A, check its tweak checkbox, then choose different tweakable item B from the same `dt-equip-cat` select.
- **Observable consequence:** At change time the select already contains B while the old checked checkbox is still present. `collectResponses()` therefore pairs B's id with `'true'`, and `renderForm()` immediately renders B checked. The code comment claims the re-render tracks the current item “not a stale one,” but the request itself is stale and silently changes target.
- **Confidence:** High. The full collection loop and delegated change branch establish the event-order/data pairing; the saved state is keyed only by slot, not catalogue id.

### [Pass 2] Stat-less `skill_gear` rows are valid but still receive a bonus-dice tweak UI

- **Severity:** Medium
- **File:line:** `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:395`; `server/schemas/equipment_catalogue.schema.js:47`; `public/js/admin/equipment-catalogue-admin.js:287`
- **Triggering input or sequence:** Create `skill_gear` with its optional `bonus_dice` input blank, or load an existing/legacy row with `bonus_dice: null`, then select it in the downtime form.
- **Observable consequence:** The schema requires only `bucket` and `name`; the admin input is optional and serializes blank as `null`. `equipmentTweakableField` checks only the bucket, returns `bonus_dice`, and renders a request to add 1 to a numeric field the item does not have. This contradicts the helper's “has a tweakable numeric bonus” contract.
- **Confidence:** High. The valid input shape is confirmed by the schema/admin code, and direct execution returned `bonus_dice` for `{ bucket: 'skill_gear' }`.

## Low

### [Pass 2] Unit coverage omits both catalogue shapes that expose the helper defects

- **Severity:** Low
- **File:line:** `server/tests/issue-879-defence-penalty-wirein.test.js:615`
- **Triggering input or sequence:** Regress either ambiguous-combat handling or the assumption that every `skill_gear` row has `bonus_dice` while retaining the currently tested weapon-only, armour-only, neither-combat, and populated-skill fixtures.
- **Observable consequence:** The suite remains green because it has no combat fixture with both shape subsets and no skill fixture with missing/null `bonus_dice`. The helper defects remain unguarded even though both shapes are valid under the real catalogue schema/editor.
- **Confidence:** High.

### Pass 2 checks that produced no finding

- `tweakedAvailability` and `rawMax` use raw availability units on both sides. For non-negative catalogue availability, `raw + 1 > cap + fixer` is exactly equivalent to `max(0, raw + 1 - fixer) > cap`; direct fixtures with and without Fixer produced identical warning decisions.
- Removing row 2 of 3 correctly copies row 3's tweak value into slot 2 inside the same loop as the other keys, then deletes the old last-slot key.
- An empty row's stored `equipment_${n}_tweak: 'false'` does not make it count as used: `dt-action-summary.js` checks only catalogue id or legacy name, and `dt-completeness.js` does not inspect equipment keys.
- `dt-equip-cat` occurs on exactly the rendered catalogue select and the delegated matcher; none of the later change-handler matchers also match that select, so the early return does not suppress another applicable branch.
- A deleted/unloaded catalogue id degrades to `getCatalogueEntry(...) === null`, leaving `tweakField` null and rendering no checkbox without dereferencing the missing entry.
- Real availability is integer-or-null by schema and the admin coerces it to a number. The new unit fixture field names match the catalogue shape; omitting `_id` does not affect either pure helper.
- The split import is justified: issue #896 asserts the original import's brace contents exactly, while the new separate import contains both new names and both are used.

+- **Observable consequence:** The test still passes although checked state is no longer persisted. Its title says it verifies persistence “from the checkbox DOM state,” but its sole regex asserts only that an assignment exists.
+- **Confidence:** High.

+# EQC-4 adversarial review findings
+
+## High
+
+### Pass 1
+
+- None found.
+
+## Medium
+
+### Pass 1
+
+#### [Pass 1] A checked tweak request follows the row, not the selected catalogue item
+
+- **Severity**: Medium
+- **File:line**: `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2781`, `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:5609`
+- **Triggering input or sequence**: In one equipment row, select tweakable item A, check `equipment_${n}_tweak`, then change the same row's catalogue dropdown to a different tweakable item B. The delegated change handler calls `collectResponses()` before rerendering, so it saves `'true'`; `renderEquipmentRow` then restores that value solely from the row-number key.
+- **Observable consequence**: Item B is immediately rendered with a checked tweak request even though the player only checked the control while item A was selected. The submitted request can therefore ask the ST to tweak a different item without a fresh affirmative action by the player.
+- **Confidence**: High from the control flow visible in the diff; whether product scope considers row-level carryover acceptable cannot be determined without the story.
+
+#### [Pass 1] Dual-shaped combat gear is silently and irreversibly treated as a weapon
+
+- **Severity**: Medium
+- **File:line**: `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:384`
+- **Triggering input or sequence**: Pass a `combat_gear` entry with any populated weapon discriminator (`weapon_type`, `damage_mod`, or `damage_type`) and any populated armour discriminator (`armour_value` or `defence_penalty`).
+- **Observable consequence**: `equipmentTweakableField` returns `damage_mod`; there is no route to request an `armour_value` tweak for the same entry. If the catalogue/admin layer permits hybrid or legacy rows, this is a silent loss of one plausible interpretation.
+- **Confidence**: Medium. The precedence is certain from the diff; whether mutual exclusivity is guaranteed elsewhere must be checked in Pass 2.
+
+## Low
+
+### Pass 1
+
+#### [Pass 1] Skill gear is declared tweakable even when it has no numeric bonus field
+
+- **Severity**: Low
+- **File:line**: `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:388`
+- **Triggering input or sequence**: Call `equipmentTweakableField({ bucket: 'skill_gear' })`, or use a malformed/legacy skill-gear catalogue row with no `bonus_dice` value.
+- **Observable consequence**: The function returns `bonus_dice` and the form offers a `+1 bonus_dice` request despite the function documentation saying it returns `null` when there is no tweakable numeric bonus. The new unit test only covers a skill-gear fixture where `bonus_dice` is present.
+- **Confidence**: Medium pending the repository's schema/admin guarantees.
+
+#### [Pass 1] Numeric-string availability is silently treated as zero
+
+- **Severity**: Low
+- **File:line**: `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:404`
+- **Triggering input or sequence**: Call `tweakedAvailability` with a tweakable entry whose availability is a numeric string, for example `{ bucket: 'skill_gear', bonus_dice: 1, availability: '3' }`.
+- **Observable consequence**: `Number.isInteger('3')` is false, so the reported tweak cost is `1` rather than `4`; the over-cap warning can consequently be suppressed. The tests cover a number and a missing value, but not the numeric-string boundary.
+- **Confidence**: Medium pending confirmation of real catalogue-document types in Pass 2.
+
+#### [Pass 1] The “ONLY when tweakable” render test does not prove conditional gating
+
+- **Severity**: Low
+- **File:line**: `server/tests/issue-871-876-ecm-4-9-bundle.test.js:164`
+- **Triggering input or sequence**: Move or duplicate the checkbox markup into unconditional render code anywhere after the first textual occurrence of `equipmentTweakableField(selectedEntry)`, while leaving that function call present.
+- **Observable consequence**: The test still passes because it checks only that the function-call text exists and that checkbox text occurs later in the file. A regression that shows the checkbox for non-tweakable items would not be caught despite the test title's “ONLY” claim.
+- **Confidence**: High.
+
+#### [Pass 1] The persistence test proves only that some assignment exists
+
+- **Severity**: Low
+- **File:line**: `server/tests/issue-871-876-ecm-4-9-bundle.test.js:180`
+- **Triggering input or sequence**: Replace the right-hand side of the tweak response assignment with a constant or invert the checkbox state while retaining `responses[`equipment_${n}_tweak`] =`.
+- **Observable consequence**: The test remains green even though checked/unchecked DOM state is no longer persisted correctly.
+- **Confidence**: High.
+
+#### [Pass 1] The availability-warning comparison cannot be unit-validated from the scoped diff
+
+- **Severity**: Low
+- **File:line**: `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:5610`
+- **Triggering input or sequence**: Render any tweakable item near the character cap; the new code compares raw `entry.availability + 1` with the pre-existing `rawMax`, whose definition is outside the diff.
+- **Observable consequence**: If `rawMax` is in effective/post-Fixer units rather than raw catalogue units, the warning threshold will be off by the Fixer adjustment. The diff alone is insufficient to decide whether this occurs.
+- **Confidence**: Low until Pass 2 traces `rawMax`, `availabilityCap`, and `fixerReduction`.
+
+#### [Pass 1] The delegated class trigger's exclusivity cannot be established from the diff
+
+- **Severity**: Low
+- **File:line**: `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2781`
+- **Triggering input or sequence**: Change any element carrying `dt-equip-cat`; the new branch collects responses and rerenders the whole form, then returns.
+- **Observable consequence**: If the class is reused, an unrelated change would spuriously rerender and the early return could suppress a later matching branch. The unchanged select markup and the rest of the large delegate are not in the diff, so exclusivity is not yet verifiable.
+- **Confidence**: Low until Pass 2 searches the real file.

+# Pass 2 — Edge Case Hunter (frozen before reading the story)
+
+## High
+
+### [Pass 2] The captured tweak request is invisible in the ST processing UI
+
+- **Severity:** High
+- **File:line:** `public/js/admin/downtime-views.js:1647`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** A player selects a tweakable catalogue item, checks `equipment_1_tweak`, and lets the form auto-save or submits it; an ST then opens that submission in the normal downtime processing UI.
+- **Observable consequence:** The response bag retains `equipment_1_tweak: 'true'`, but `renderPlayerResponses` builds each equipment row from only catalogue id/name, quantity, and notes. The only repository references to the new response key are the player-form write/render/slot-shift sites, so the ST sees an ordinary equipment request and has no indication that the player requested a +1 stat tweak. The feature's own player copy says the ST will adjudicate it, but the ST-facing surface drops the signal.
+- **Confidence:** High. The complete equipment renderer was inspected and a repository-wide source search found no downstream reader of `equipment_${n}_tweak`.
+
+## Medium
+
+### [Pass 2] Dual-shaped combat gear is supported by the catalogue editor but has only a weapon tweak path
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:390`; `public/js/admin/equipment-catalogue-admin.js:32`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** An ST creates or edits `combat_gear` with both a weapon field and an armour field populated—for example, `damage_mod: 1` and `armour_value: 2`—then a player selects it in an equipment-acquisition row.
+- **Observable consequence:** The admin module explicitly says both subsets may be populated “in principle,” renders all five weapon/armour inputs together, and performs no mutual-exclusivity validation. Nevertheless, `equipmentTweakableField` returns `damage_mod` at the first predicate and never offers an armour-value tweak. A supported catalogue row therefore loses one of its two plausible tweak choices by branch order alone.
+- **Confidence:** High. Direct execution returned `damage_mod` for the dual-shaped fixture, and both the schema and admin form permit that fixture.
+
+### [Pass 2] A checked request still migrates when the catalogue selection changes
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2785`; `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:5613`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** In one row, select tweakable item A, check its tweak checkbox, then choose different tweakable item B from the same `dt-equip-cat` select.
+- **Observable consequence:** At change time the select already contains B while the old checked checkbox is still present. `collectResponses()` therefore pairs B's id with `'true'`, and `renderForm()` immediately renders B checked. The code comment claims the re-render tracks the current item “not a stale one,” but the request itself is stale and silently changes target.
+- **Confidence:** High. The full collection loop and delegated change branch establish the event-order/data pairing; the saved state is keyed only by slot, not catalogue id.
+
+### [Pass 2] Stat-less `skill_gear` rows are valid but still receive a bonus-dice tweak UI
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:395`; `server/schemas/equipment_catalogue.schema.js:47`; `public/js/admin/equipment-catalogue-admin.js:287`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Create `skill_gear` with its optional `bonus_dice` input blank, or load an existing/legacy row with `bonus_dice: null`, then select it in the downtime form.
+- **Observable consequence:** The schema requires only `bucket` and `name`; the admin input is optional and serializes blank as `null`. `equipmentTweakableField` checks only the bucket, returns `bonus_dice`, and renders a request to add 1 to a numeric field the item does not have. This contradicts the helper's “has a tweakable numeric bonus” contract.
+- **Confidence:** High. The valid input shape is confirmed by the schema/admin code, and direct execution returned `bonus_dice` for `{ bucket: 'skill_gear' }`.
+
+### [Pass 2] An availability-5 tweak produces a cost the catalogue cannot represent
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:407`; `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:5612`; `server/schemas/equipment_catalogue.schema.js:58`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Select a tweakable catalogue item with raw `availability: 5`; for the sharpest case, use a character with Resources 5 and Fixer, making `rawMax` 6.
+- **Observable consequence:** `tweakedAvailability` returns 6 and the form displays availability 6. For Resources 5 + Fixer, `6 > 6` is false, so no warning appears, yet the catalogue schema/admin cap availability at 5 and the form comment says adjudicated granting uses a distinct catalogue entry. That advertised representation cannot store the computed request cost.
+- **Confidence:** High about the code/schema mismatch; Medium about whether the story defines special handling for above-scale requests.
+
+## Low
+
+### [Pass 2] Unit coverage omits both catalogue shapes that expose the helper defects
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `server/tests/issue-879-defence-penalty-wirein.test.js:615`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Regress either ambiguous-combat handling or the assumption that every `skill_gear` row has `bonus_dice` while retaining the currently tested weapon-only, armour-only, neither-combat, and populated-skill fixtures.
+- **Observable consequence:** The suite remains green because it has no combat fixture with both shape subsets and no skill fixture with missing/null `bonus_dice`. The helper defects remain unguarded even though both shapes are valid under the real catalogue schema/editor.
+- **Confidence:** High.
+
+### Pass 2 checks that produced no finding
+
+- `tweakedAvailability` and `rawMax` use raw availability units on both sides. For non-negative catalogue availability, `raw + 1 > cap + fixer` is exactly equivalent to `max(0, raw + 1 - fixer) > cap`; direct fixtures with and without Fixer produced identical warning decisions.
+- Removing row 2 of 3 correctly copies row 3's tweak value into slot 2 inside the same loop as the other keys, then deletes the old last-slot key.
+- An empty row's stored `equipment_${n}_tweak: 'false'` does not make it count as used: `dt-action-summary.js` checks only catalogue id or legacy name, and `dt-completeness.js` does not inspect equipment keys.
+- `dt-equip-cat` occurs on exactly the rendered catalogue select and the delegated matcher; none of the later change-handler matchers also match that select, so the early return does not suppress another applicable branch.
+- A deleted/unloaded catalogue id degrades to `getCatalogueEntry(...) === null`, leaving `tweakField` null and rendering no checkbox without dereferencing the missing entry.
+- Real availability is integer-or-null by schema and the admin coerces it to a number. The new unit fixture field names match the catalogue shape; omitting `_id` does not affect either pure helper.
+- The split import is justified: issue #896 asserts the original import's brace contents exactly, while the new separate import contains both new names and both are used.
+
+# Pass 3a — Acceptance Auditor (frozen before reading the Dev Agent Record)
+
+## High
+
+### [Pass 3a] The core story promise that the ST can see the structured request is not delivered
+
+- **Severity:** High
+- **File:line:** `specs/stories/feature.1155.eqc4-purchase-stat-tweak.story.md:18`; `public/js/admin/downtime-views.js:1647`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** A player checks a tweak request and saves/submits, then the ST reviews the submission through TM Suite's downtime processing UI.
+- **Observable consequence:** The Story explicitly requires a structured request “the ST can see and adjudicate,” but the ST renderer never reads `equipment_${n}_tweak`. The player-facing data is stored yet indistinguishable from a normal acquisition in the adjudication surface, so the stated user outcome is absent.
+- **Confidence:** High. This is a literal Story mismatch backed by the complete downstream renderer and repository-wide source search.
+
+## Medium
+
+### [Pass 3a] Changing items violates AC #3's “unchecked by default” requirement
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `specs/stories/feature.1155.eqc4-purchase-stat-tweak.story.md:73`; `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2785`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Select tweakable item A, check its request, then switch the same row to different tweakable item B.
+- **Observable consequence:** B's newly rendered checkbox is checked because collection preserves the slot-level `'true'` value. AC #3 says the checkbox is unchecked by default, and AC #4 says the dependent UI must track the currently selected item rather than stale state; this sequence carries A's explicit choice into B without a fresh choice.
+- **Confidence:** High.
+
+### [Pass 3a] AC #5's warning is shown before the player checks the tweak request
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `specs/stories/feature.1155.eqc4-purchase-stat-tweak.story.md:81`; `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:5613`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** A character selects a tweakable item whose +1 cost is over the affordability threshold and leaves the newly rendered checkbox unchecked.
+- **Observable consequence:** AC #5 scopes the warning to “When the tweak checkbox is checked,” but `warning` depends only on `tweakCost > rawMax`; `tweakChecked` affects only the checkbox attribute. The row warns immediately for a request the player has not made. Checking/unchecking also schedules a save without re-rendering, so warning visibility cannot track checked state at runtime.
+- **Confidence:** High.
+
+## Low
+
+### [Pass 3a] `tweakedAvailability` narrows AC #2's nullish-default formula to integers
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `specs/stories/feature.1155.eqc4-purchase-stat-tweak.story.md:70`; `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:409`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** A shared-module caller passes a tweakable partial with a non-nullish, non-integer availability, such as `{ bucket: 'skill_gear', availability: 2.5 }` or a numeric string from an uncoerced form.
+- **Observable consequence:** AC #2 literally specifies `(entry.availability ?? 0) + 1`; the implementation instead replaces every non-integer with 0 and returns 1. Current persisted catalogue documents are integer-or-null, so the normal DT path is unaffected, but the exported shared helper does not implement its stated input formula for partial/future callers.
+- **Confidence:** High on the literal discrepancy; Low-to-Medium on runtime impact because the current catalogue schema/admin path supplies integer-or-null.
+
+### Pass 3a checks that produced no finding
+
+- AC #5's comparison is not a units bug for valid catalogue data. Although the code compares raw tweaked cost with `rawMax = availabilityCap + fixerReduction`, that inequality is decision-equivalent to comparing Fixer-adjusted tweaked cost with `availabilityCap`; the warning fires at the same boundary.
+- AC #1 explicitly says every `skill_gear` entry returns `bonus_dice`, so Pass 2's stat-less-skill concern is a robustness/domain-contract concern, not a deviation from AC #1. The earlier frozen finding remains unchanged as required.
+- AC #1 does not define precedence for a combat entry satisfying both shape predicates, so it does not resolve the dual-shaped ambiguity found in Passes 1/2.
+- The implementation adds no character-equipment schema field, automated grant, downward or stacked tweak, or tweak surface for `tool_utility`/`narrative`/`container`; it also leaves the existing dropdown filtering loop unchanged.
+- `git diff --name-status 41dd40ef -- .` listed only the two TM Suite source files and two tests from the supplied diff. No tracked TM Wiki, TM Cockpit, or TM Herald path is touched; sibling worktrees were not accessed.

+- **File:line:** `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:395`; `server/schemas/equipment_catalogue.schema.js:47`; `public/js/admin/equipment-catalogue-admin.js:287`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Create `skill_gear` with its optional `bonus_dice` input blank, or load an existing/legacy row with `bonus_dice: null`, then select it in the downtime form.
+- **Observable consequence:** The schema requires only `bucket` and `name`; the admin input is optional and serializes blank as `null`. `equipmentTweakableField` checks only the bucket, returns `bonus_dice`, and renders a request to add 1 to a numeric field the item does not have. This contradicts the helper's “has a tweakable numeric bonus” contract.
+- **Confidence:** High. The valid input shape is confirmed by the schema/admin code, and direct execution returned `bonus_dice` for `{ bucket: 'skill_gear' }`.
+
+### [Pass 2] An availability-5 tweak produces a cost the catalogue cannot represent
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:407`; `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:5612`; `server/schemas/equipment_catalogue.schema.js:58`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Select a tweakable catalogue item with raw `availability: 5`; for the sharpest case, use a character with Resources 5 and Fixer, making `rawMax` 6.
+- **Observable consequence:** `tweakedAvailability` returns 6 and the form displays availability 6. For Resources 5 + Fixer, `6 > 6` is false, so no warning appears, yet the catalogue schema/admin cap availability at 5 and the form comment says adjudicated granting uses a distinct catalogue entry. That advertised representation cannot store the computed request cost.
+- **Confidence:** High about the code/schema mismatch; Medium about whether the story defines special handling for above-scale requests.
+
+## Low
+
+### [Pass 2] Unit coverage omits both catalogue shapes that expose the helper defects
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `server/tests/issue-879-defence-penalty-wirein.test.js:615`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Regress either ambiguous-combat handling or the assumption that every `skill_gear` row has `bonus_dice` while retaining the currently tested weapon-only, armour-only, neither-combat, and populated-skill fixtures.
+- **Observable consequence:** The suite remains green because it has no combat fixture with both shape subsets and no skill fixture with missing/null `bonus_dice`. The helper defects remain unguarded even though both shapes are valid under the real catalogue schema/editor.
+- **Confidence:** High.
+
+### Pass 2 checks that produced no finding
+
+- `tweakedAvailability` and `rawMax` use raw availability units on both sides. For non-negative catalogue availability, `raw + 1 > cap + fixer` is exactly equivalent to `max(0, raw + 1 - fixer) > cap`; direct fixtures with and without Fixer produced identical warning decisions.
+- Removing row 2 of 3 correctly copies row 3's tweak value into slot 2 inside the same loop as the other keys, then deletes the old last-slot key.
+- An empty row's stored `equipment_${n}_tweak: 'false'` does not make it count as used: `dt-action-summary.js` checks only catalogue id or legacy name, and `dt-completeness.js` does not inspect equipment keys.
+- `dt-equip-cat` occurs on exactly the rendered catalogue select and the delegated matcher; none of the later change-handler matchers also match that select, so the early return does not suppress another applicable branch.
+- A deleted/unloaded catalogue id degrades to `getCatalogueEntry(...) === null`, leaving `tweakField` null and rendering no checkbox without dereferencing the missing entry.
+- Real availability is integer-or-null by schema and the admin coerces it to a number. The new unit fixture field names match the catalogue shape; omitting `_id` does not affect either pure helper.
+- The split import is justified: issue #896 asserts the original import's brace contents exactly, while the new separate import contains both new names and both are used.

+### [Pass 3a] Changing items violates AC #3's “unchecked by default” requirement
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `specs/stories/feature.1155.eqc4-purchase-stat-tweak.story.md:73`; `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2785`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Select tweakable item A, check its request, then switch the same row to different tweakable item B.
+- **Observable consequence:** B's newly rendered checkbox is checked because collection preserves the slot-level `'true'` value. AC #3 says the checkbox is unchecked by default, and AC #4 says the dependent UI must track the currently selected item rather than stale state; this sequence carries A's explicit choice into B without a fresh choice.
+- **Confidence:** High.

+### [Pass 3a] AC #5's warning is shown before the player checks the tweak request
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `specs/stories/feature.1155.eqc4-purchase-stat-tweak.story.md:81`; `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:5613`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** A character selects a tweakable item whose +1 cost is over the affordability threshold and leaves the newly rendered checkbox unchecked.
+- **Observable consequence:** AC #5 scopes the warning to “When the tweak checkbox is checked,” but `warning` depends only on `tweakCost > rawMax`; `tweakChecked` affects only the checkbox attribute. The row warns immediately for a request the player has not made. Checking/unchecking also schedules a save without re-rendering, so warning visibility cannot track checked state at runtime.
+- **Confidence:** High.

+### [Pass 3a] `tweakedAvailability` narrows AC #2's nullish-default formula to integers
+

+- **Triggering input or sequence:** A shared-module caller passes a tweakable partial with a non-nullish, non-integer availability, such as `{ bucket: 'skill_gear', availability: 2.5 }` or a numeric string from an uncoerced form.
+- **Observable consequence:** AC #2 literally specifies `(entry.availability ?? 0) + 1`; the implementation instead replaces every non-integer with 0 and returns 1. Current persisted catalogue documents are integer-or-null, so the normal DT path is unaffected, but the exported shared helper does not implement its stated input formula for partial/future callers.
+- **Confidence:** High on the literal discrepancy; Low-to-Medium on runtime impact because the current catalogue schema/admin path supplies integer-or-null.

+### Pass 3a checks that produced no finding
+
+- AC #5's comparison is not a units bug for valid catalogue data. Although the code compares raw tweaked cost with `rawMax = availabilityCap + fixerReduction`, that inequality is decision-equivalent to comparing Fixer-adjusted tweaked cost with `availabilityCap`; the warning fires at the same boundary.
+- AC #1 explicitly says every `skill_gear` entry returns `bonus_dice`, so Pass 2's stat-less-skill concern is a robustness/domain-contract concern, not a deviation from AC #1. The earlier frozen finding remains unchanged as required.
+- AC #1 does not define precedence for a combat entry satisfying both shape predicates, so it does not resolve the dual-shaped ambiguity found in Passes 1/2.
+- The implementation adds no character-equipment schema field, automated grant, downward or stacked tweak, or tweak surface for `tool_utility`/`narrative`/`container`; it also leaves the existing dropdown filtering loop unchanged.

The delegated change handler calls `collectResponses()` before rerendering, so it saves `'true'`; `renderEquipmentRow` then restores that value solely from the row-number key.
+- **Observable consequence**: Item B is immediately rendered with a checked tweak request even though the player only checked the control while item A was selected. The submitted request can therefore ask the ST to tweak a different item without a fresh affirmative action by the player.
+- **Confidence**: High from the control flow visible in the diff; whether product scope considers row-level carryover acceptable cannot be determined without the story.

+- **Observable consequence**: `equipmentTweakableField` returns `damage_mod`; there is no route to request an `armour_value` tweak for the same entry. If the catalogue/admin layer permits hybrid or legacy rows, this is a silent loss of one plausible interpretation.

+### [Pass 2] The captured tweak request is invisible in the ST processing UI
+
+- **Severity:** High
+- **File:line:** `public/js/admin/downtime-views.js:1647`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** A player selects a tweakable catalogue item, checks `equipment_1_tweak`, and lets the form auto-save or submits it; an ST then opens that submission in the normal downtime processing UI.
+- **Observable consequence:** The response bag retains `equipment_1_tweak: 'true'`, but `renderPlayerResponses` builds each equipment row from only catalogue id/name, quantity, and notes. The only repository references to the new response key are the player-form write/render/slot-shift sites, so the ST sees an ordinary equipment request and has no indication that the player requested a +1 stat tweak. The feature's own player copy says the ST will adjudicate it, but the ST-facing surface drops the signal.
+- **Confidence:** High. The complete equipment renderer was inspected and a repository-wide source search found no downstream reader of `equipment_${n}_tweak`.

+## Medium
+
+### [Pass 2] Dual-shaped combat gear is supported by the catalogue editor but has only a weapon tweak path
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:390`; `public/js/admin/equipment-catalogue-admin.js:32`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** An ST creates or edits `combat_gear` with both a weapon field and an armour field populated—for example, `damage_mod: 1` and `armour_value: 2`—then a player selects it in an equipment-acquisition row.
+- **Observable consequence:** The admin module explicitly says both subsets may be populated “in principle,” renders all five weapon/armour inputs together, and performs no mutual-exclusivity validation. Nevertheless, `equipmentTweakableField` returns `damage_mod` at the first predicate and never offers an armour-value tweak. A supported catalogue row therefore loses one of its two plausible tweak choices by branch order alone.
+- **Confidence:** High. Direct execution returned `damage_mod` for the dual-shaped fixture, and both the schema and admin form permit that fixture.

+### [Pass 2] A checked request still migrates when the catalogue selection changes
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:2785`; `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:5613`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** In one row, select tweakable item A, check its tweak checkbox, then choose different tweakable item B from the same `dt-equip-cat` select.
+- **Observable consequence:** At change time the select already contains B while the old checked checkbox is still present. `collectResponses()` therefore pairs B's id with `'true'`, and `renderForm()` immediately renders B checked. The code comment claims the re-render tracks the current item “not a stale one,” but the request itself is stale and silently changes target.
+- **Confidence:** High. The full collection loop and delegated change branch establish the event-order/data pairing; the saved state is keyed only by slot, not catalogue id.

+### [Pass 2] Stat-less `skill_gear` rows are valid but still receive a bonus-dice tweak UI
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:395`; `server/schemas/equipment_catalogue.schema.js:47`; `public/js/admin/equipment-catalogue-admin.js:287`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Create `skill_gear` with its optional `bonus_dice` input blank, or load an existing/legacy row with `bonus_dice: null`, then select it in the downtime form.
+- **Observable consequence:** The schema requires only `bucket` and `name`; the admin input is optional and serializes blank as `null`. `equipmentTweakableField` checks only the bucket, returns `bonus_dice`, and renders a request to add 1 to a numeric field the item does not have. This contradicts the helper's “has a tweakable numeric bonus” contract.
+- **Confidence:** High. The valid input shape is confirmed by the schema/admin code, and direct execution returned `bonus_dice` for `{ bucket: 'skill_gear' }`.
+
+### [Pass 2] An availability-5 tweak produces a cost the catalogue cannot represent
+
+- **Severity:** Medium
+- **File:line:** `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:407`; `public/js/tabs/downtime-form.js:5612`; `server/schemas/equipment_catalogue.schema.js:58`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Select a tweakable catalogue item with raw `availability: 5`; for the sharpest case, use a character with Resources 5 and Fixer, making `rawMax` 6.
+- **Observable consequence:** `tweakedAvailability` returns 6 and the form displays availability 6. For Resources 5 + Fixer, `6 > 6` is false, so no warning appears, yet the catalogue schema/admin cap availability at 5 and the form comment says adjudicated granting uses a distinct catalogue entry. That advertised representation cannot store the computed request cost.
+- **Confidence:** High about the code/schema mismatch; Medium about whether the story defines special handling for above-scale requests.

+## Low

+### [Pass 2] Unit coverage omits both catalogue shapes that expose the helper defects
+
+- **Severity:** Low
+- **File:line:** `server/tests/issue-879-defence-penalty-wirein.test.js:615`
+- **Triggering input or sequence:** Regress either ambiguous-combat handling or the assumption that every `skill_gear` row has `bonus_dice` while retaining the currently tested weapon-only, armour-only, neither-combat, and populated-skill fixtures.
+- **Observable consequence:** The suite remains green because it has no combat fixture with both shape subsets and no skill fixture with missing/null `bonus_dice`. The helper defects remain unguarded even though both shapes are valid under the real catalogue schema/editor.

+
+### Pass 2 checks that produced no finding
+
+- `tweakedAvailability` and `rawMax` use raw availability units on both sides. For non-negative catalogue availability, `raw + 1 > cap + fixer` is exactly equivalent to `max(0, raw + 1 - fixer) > cap`; direct fixtures with and without Fixer produced identical warning decisions.
+- Removing row 2 of 3 correctly copies row 3's tweak value into slot 2 inside the same loop as the other keys, then deletes the old last-slot key.
+- An empty row's stored `equipment_${n}_tweak: 'false'` does not make it count as used: `dt-action-summary.js` checks only catalogue id or legacy name, and `dt-completeness.js` does not inspect equipment keys.
+- `dt-equip-cat` occurs on exactly the rendered catalogue select and the delegated matcher; none of the later change-handler matchers also match that select, so the early return does not suppress another applicable branch.
+- A deleted/unloaded catalogue id degrades to `getCatalogueEntry(...) === null`, leaving `tweakField` null and rendering no checkbox without dereferencing the missing entry.
+- Real availability is integer-or-null by schema and the admin coerces it to a number. The new unit fixture field names match the catalogue shape; omitting `_id` does not affect either pure helper.
+- The split import is justified: issue #896 asserts the original import's brace contents exactly, while the new separate import contains both new names and both are used.

  11: ---
  12: 
  13: ## Story
  14: 
  15: **As a** player filing a downtime equipment acquisition,
  16: **I want** to optionally request a one-step stat tweak on the item I'm acquiring, paying one extra
  17: availability dot for it,
  18: **so that** minor customisation ("this pistol, but +1 damage") is a structured, capped request the ST
  19: can see and adjudicate — not an ad hoc negotiation with no anti-cheese guardrail.
  20: 
  21: ## Background
  22: 
  23: Epic #1038 item 5: *"Programmatic purchasing: pick from the catalogue, availability vs resources
  24: checked automatically. Stat tweaks allowed at one dot of availability per shift, limited to one step
  25: per stat (anti micro-sword cheese). Per Peter, the stat-shift constraint is ~3 lines."*
  26: 
  27: **Investigation finding, this session**: "availability vs resources checked automatically" is already
  28: built — issue #896 (`isAffordable`/`availabilityCap`/`effectiveAvailability`) already gates the DT
  29: form's equipment dropdown, disabling options a character can't afford (Resources rating + Fixer
  30: reduction). The genuinely new piece is the stat-tweak request.
  31: 
  32: **Scope decision (Angelus, via AskUserQuestion, this session)**: tweakable stats are the ONE primary
  33: numeric bonus field per bucket-shape a purchased item actually has — `damage_mod` for weapon-shaped
  34: `combat_gear`, `armour_value` for armour-shaped `combat_gear`, `bonus_dice` for `skill_gear`.
  35: `tool_utility` (no numeric bonus by design — "does a thing, no bonus"), `narrative`, and `container`
  36: items have no tweakable field at all. This means every tweakable item has exactly ONE tweakable stat,
  37: so "one step per stat" collapses to "one tweak, always +1, on the one number that matters" for this
  38: scope — matching Peter's own "~3 lines" sizing.
  39: 
  40: **Architecture decision**: this codebase's equipment rows are deliberately lean references
  41: (`catalogue_id` only — "full stats resolved at render time", EQ-1's own founding design rule, repeated
  42: in every equipment schema comment since). A tweaked item therefore does NOT get a stat-override field
  43: on the equipment row — that would fork this architecture for one feature. Instead, granting a tweaked
  44: item means the ST creates a DISTINCT catalogue entry for the tweaked variant (e.g. "Glock 17 (+1
  45: dmg)") via the catalogue-admin CRUD that already exists (EQC-1), same as creating any other new
  46: catalogue item. This story is scoped to the REQUEST side only — capturing what a player is asking for,
  47: structured and capped — not the granting side, which needs no new infrastructure.
  48: 
  49: ## Explicitly NOT this story
  50: 
  51: - **No new schema field.** No stat-override on `character.equipment[]` rows. See Architecture decision.
  52: - **No automated granting.** An ST still manually creates the tweaked catalogue variant and assigns it
  53:   via existing tooling (equipment-catalogue-admin.js CRUD + the equipment-add flow from EQC-1/EQC-3).
  54:   This story only structures the REQUEST.
  55: - **No downward tweaks.** The mechanic is "pay more, get a better stat" (anti micro-sword cheese is
  56:   about capping UPGRADES, not modelling downgrades nobody would rationally request). Always +1 to the
  57:   bucket's primary numeric stat, never −1.
  58: - **No stacking multiple tweaks on one item, and no tweaking `tool_utility`/`narrative`/`container`
  59:   items** — they have no primary numeric bonus field to tweak in the first place.
  60: - **No change to the existing affordability-gate dropdown logic for CHOOSING which items appear** —
  61:   that's #896's own established behaviour, untouched. This story adds a tweak checkbox that appears
  62:   AFTER an item is chosen, not a new filtering dimension on the dropdown itself.
  63: 
  64: ## Acceptance Criteria
  65: 
  66: 1. `equipment-derivation.js` exports `equipmentTweakableField(entry)`: returns `'damage_mod'` for a
  67:    weapon-shaped `combat_gear` entry, `'armour_value'` for an armour-shaped `combat_gear` entry,
  68:    `'bonus_dice'` for a `skill_gear` entry, `null` otherwise (including a combat_gear entry that's
  69:    neither weapon- nor armour-shaped, and every `tool_utility`/`narrative`/`container` entry).
  70: 2. `equipment-derivation.js` exports `tweakedAvailability(entry)`: returns `(entry.availability ?? 0)
  71:    + 1` when `equipmentTweakableField(entry)` is non-null, `null` when it's not tweakable at all (there
  72:    is no meaningful "tweaked cost" for an item with no tweakable stat).
  73: 3. `tabs/downtime-form.js`'s equipment acquisition row (`renderEquipmentRow`) shows a "+1 tweak"
  74:    checkbox once an item is selected, ONLY when that item is tweakable, labelled with which stat and
  75:    the resulting availability cost (e.g. "+1 damage_mod (raises cost to avail 3)"). Unchecked by
  76:    default; state persists via a new `equipment_${n}_tweak` response key (boolean-as-string, matching
  77:    the existing `qty`/`notes` field convention).
  78: 4. The row re-renders when the catalogue-item dropdown changes (new delegated-change-handler branch,
  79:    matching the existing pattern for Carthian Pull / rote dropdowns in the same file), so the tweak
  80:    checkbox's visibility tracks the CURRENTLY selected item, not a stale one.
  81: 5. When the tweak checkbox is checked and the tweaked cost (`tweakedAvailability`) exceeds the
  82:    character's effective availability cap, the row shows a warning matching the existing
  83:    over-cap-tooltip wording style (`isAffordable`-based) — informational only, does not block saving
  84:    the draft (STs adjudicate DT submissions, same as every other field in this form).
  85: 6. `npm test`: every equipment-related suite green; no new failures.
  86: 7. TM Wiki, TM Cockpit, and TM Herald are completely untouched — TM Suite-only.

The delegated change handler calls `collectResponses()` before rerendering, so it saves `'true'`; `renderEquipmentRow` then restores that value solely from the row-number key.
+- **Observable consequence**: Item B is immediately rendered with a checked tweak request even though the player only checked the control while item A was selected. The submitted request can therefore ask the ST to tweak a different item without a fresh affirmative action by the player.
+- **Confidence**: High from the control flow visible in the diff; whether product scope considers row-level carryover acceptable cannot be determined without the story.
+
+#### [Pass 1] Dual-shaped combat gear is silently and irreversibly treated as a weapon
+
+- **Severity**: Medium
+- **File:line**: `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:384`
+- **Triggering input or sequence**: Pass a `combat_gear` entry with any populated weapon discriminator (`weapon_type`, `damage_mod`, or `damage_type`) and any populated armour discriminator (`armour_value` or `defence_penalty`).
+- **Observable consequence**: `equipmentTweakableField` returns `damage_mod`; there is no route to request an `armour_value` tweak for the same entry. If the catalogue/admin layer permits hybrid or legacy rows, this is a silent loss of one plausible interpretation.
+- **Confidence**: Medium. The precedence is certain from the diff; whether mutual exclusivity is guaranteed elsewhere must be checked in Pass 2.

+- **Observable consequence**: The function returns `bonus_dice` and the form offers a `+1 bonus_dice` request despite the function documentation saying it returns `null` when there is no tweakable numeric bonus. The new unit test only covers a skill-gear fixture where `bonus_dice` is present.

+#### [Pass 1] Numeric-string availability is silently treated as zero
+
+- **Severity**: Low
+- **File:line**: `public/js/data/equipment-derivation.js:404`
+- **Triggering input or sequence**: Call `tweakedAvailability` with a tweakable entry whose availability is a numeric string, for example `{ bucket: 'skill_gear', bonus_dice: 1, availability: '3' }`.
+- **Observable consequence**: `Number.isInteger('3')` is false, so the reported tweak cost is `1` rather than `4`; the over-cap warning can consequently be suppressed. The tests cover a number and a missing value, but not the numeric-string boundary.
+- **Confidence**: Medium pending confirmation of real catalogue-document types in Pass 2.

+# Pass 2 — Edge Case Hunter (frozen before reading the story)
